title: Energy Assistance Window Anchored on the Collection Cycle of an Electric Service Agreement
content:
## Section text

For the reconnection charge on an Electric Service Agreement, energy assistance agency payments are counted over the assistance window, which is anchored on the agreement's collection history: when a reconnection charge was posted on the agreement in the 12 calendar months before the order, the window is the number of whole calendar months that have passed since the most recent such charge, so that only assistance received in the current collection cycle counts; when none was but a written disconnection notice was served in that period, the window is the 6 calendar months before the order; otherwise it is the 12 calendar months before the order.

Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date. That convention applies to the reconnection charges and written notices looked for in the 12 calendar months, and to the agency payments counted in the window.

## Window by collection history

| Collection history in the 12 calendar months before the order | Assistance window |
|---|---|
| at least 1 reconnection charge posted on the agreement | the whole calendar months passed since the most recent reconnection charge |
| no reconnection charge, at least 1 written disconnection notice served | the 6 calendar months before the order |
| neither | the 12 calendar months before the order |

A reconnection charge in the period decides the window whether or not a written notice was also served.

## Illustrations (hypothetical dates)

- An order is placed on 15 June. The most recent reconnection charge was posted on 3 February of the same year. Four whole calendar months have passed (3 February to 3 June), so the window is 4 months: an agency payment dated 20 February is counted, and one dated 10 February is not.
- An order is placed on 15 June with no reconnection charge in the prior 12 months but a written notice served in April: the window is the 6 calendar months before the order, so a payment dated 16 December of the previous year is counted and one dated 15 December is not.
- With neither a reconnection charge nor a written notice in the 12 months, payments dated less than 12 whole calendar months before the order are counted.
